about: identity.refuse / identity.flag hold salted SHA-256 hashes of InChIKey skeleton blocks, so
this file is not a readable list of structures. The salt is not a secret and is not meant to
be: it keeps the file from being a browsable catalogue, nothing more.
fingerprints.refuse holds base64 Morgan fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bits) for close-analog
screening. Both lists ship empty, because populating them means authoring a list of agent
identifiers; the loader and the matching are tested with synthetic entries instead.
alerts hold generic SMARTS for whole chemical families. Each carries its own action: refuse
for families with no therapeutic use, flag for chemotypes that are working medicine and are
only worth labelling. A flag never blocks the work.
Coverage is partial by construction. The protection that does not depend on coverage is that
no tool in this phase plans a reaction, writes a procedure, or gives a dose.

not_screenable: Protein and alkaloid toxins (ricin, abrin, saxitoxin and the like) are not usefully matched
by a small-molecule SMARTS or a Morgan fingerprint. They are out of reach of this screen;
the capability decline in decline.py is what covers requests about them, because no tool
here does anything with a protein sequence.
